result: {"lens":"COMPLETENESS_GOVERNANCE","verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","summary":"024B-core scope split is well-governed: SCOPE-CORRECTION-2026-05-09.md carries empirical R6→R7→R8 trajectory, an explicit why-not-descope section, and a carry-forward reference. The D-044 decision row cites the scope-correction doc, is scoped to core deliverables, and is filed ACCEPTED. STATUS.md split-decision entry documents the extras-parking branch and three outcome rows. The plan-doc §6 amendment gates 024C on both halves plus FUP-ACC-INSTALL-TARGET-REPO-001 (captured in the split note). VERSIONING.md alignment is clean — scaffolder, template, and CI script are internal tooling, no version bump required. Anti-descoping posture is sound; no extras-scope content leaked into core files. Code coverage of plan-doc invariant 2 is complete across all five cascade-status check-paths including the fail-closed default and adopter-slug canonicalisation. One MAJ is filed: the DISPATCH-NOTE declares cascade-status: not applicable inside a backtick markdown span (line starts with the backtick delimiter, not cascade-status:), so the enforcement script's Python regex ^cascade-status:\\s+ finds zero matches and would exit with an error if run against this file. This breaks machine-parseability of the DISPATCH-NOTE per plan-doc invariant 2 and will cause CI self-dogfood failure when 024B-extras wires the enforcement workflow. Four lower-severity findings cover the scorecard-emit true permissions gap in the template, asymmetric negative-case test coverage for the blocked-on-adopter-conflict regex path, missing manifest validation for the scorecard-emit true variant, and a stale invocation-log convention claim in the DECISIONS.md reservation header note.","findings":[{"id":"CG-R1-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"DISPATCH-NOTE cascade-status field is backtick-wrapped so the enforcement script regex cannot parse it, finding 0 matches instead of 1.","evidence":"DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 9: starts with backtick character — `cascade-status: not applicable` — not with cascade-status:. Python regex ^cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$ with re.M anchors to line-start and finds 0 matches, triggering the exactly-one-match error exit. test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh case 15b uses a bare cascade-status: not applicable at line start as the passing fixture, confirming required format.","impact":"When 024B-extras ships the CI enforcement workflow, any PR that checks the 024B-core DISPATCH-NOTE exits non-zero. Also establishes a formatting precedent that would silently break cascade-slice self-dogfood if copied.","mitigation":"Add a bare cascade-status: not applicable line at the start of a line in the DISPATCH-NOTE (no backtick prefix), replacing or preceding the backtick-formatted inline-code span, so the regex finds exactly one match."},{"id":"CG-R1-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"Template adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl has no inline comment warning that scorecard-emit: true requires additional permissions not present in the template.","evidence":"Template lines 9-12: permissions block emits only contents: read + statuses: write regardless of {{SCORECARD_EMIT}}.
